cohort: A 16-year-old boy diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder, exhibiting an IQ in the lower part of the normal range but high-functioning memory skills.
finding: A microdeletion encompassing pseudogene chr14.232.a, which encodes lncLRFN5-10, was found to affect the expression levels of the nearby, non-deleted LRFN5 gene in a patient with ASD, illustrating a potential role of lncRNAs in regulating gene expression in ASD pathogenesis.
